text:
jason: Noticing mismatch between console per-token burn and backend econ for routes using sticky routing + prefix cache. Console shows ~30% lower burn. Anyone else?

tara: Yep saw a blip yesterday on canary. My hypothesis: console amortizes cache savings across session windows, backend attributes savings per-invocation.

cheng: Can you paste a minimal example (route id + sample invocation) so I can look in the logs?

jason: Sure — copied from the trace.

route: /api/chat
route_id: r_84f
invocation_id: inv_20260318_01
user_id: u_912
model_preferred: redwood/vicuna-13b-q4
decision_path: router->sticky(tenantA)->prefetch->serve(prefetch_hit)
tokens_in: 120
tokens_out: 320
console_unit_cost_est: $0.012
backend_econ_event_cost: $0.017
notes: backend shows fallback to vicuna-7b for tail, console shows amortized savings to vicuna-13b

sylvia: That pattern matches an existing edge case. Router prefetch credits are currently tagged with the original route/model pair; later fallbacks that actually serve the tail get charged per-invocation in the backend. Console aggregates prefetch credits into the route's hour window, so it looks cheaper.

aj: Two problems: (1) mismatch in attribution semantics, (2) sampling differences. Console uses 1/100 sample rate for detailed econ, backend billing uses full-sample.

tara: For immediate UX fix we could add an explainability tooltip: "Console uses session-amortized cache credits; backend shows per-invocation cost" with a link to docs. That should reduce ops noise while we change the API.

cheng: API change proposal (minimal): emit per-request telemetry field `cache_credit_source` and `cache_credit_value` in the router -> telemetry pipeline. That lets console reconstruct both amortized and per-invocation views. Low risk.

jason: Sounds good. Any objections to adding both fields to telemetry v2?

sylvia: No objections. We should also add a deterministic tie-breaker: if fallback occurs, mark `served_model` and `claimed_prefetch_model` so we can attribute properly.

aj: Caveat: exposing `cache_credit_value` to console will surface noise to non-technical users. UX should default to 'unit-econ (amortized)' but offer 'per-invocation' toggle.

tara: I'll draft a quick mock for the toggle and a 'why difference' modal that links to the telemetry fields.

cheng: I'll open the telemetry PR today. Plan: add fields, wire to incoming ingest, and add a flag `econ_v2=true` for canary.

deploy-bot: deployed telemetry-v2 canary to staging at 1736001300 :rocket:

jason: Great — once canary is up let's run a small replay on tenantA traces and compare console vs backend for 2 hours.

aj: Scheduling quick sync with product tom 10:30 to agree on default UX and rollout cadence.

tara: +1 :thumbsup:
